A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
resistance to FHB in the Czech winter wheat varieties is low and that it is not possible to find a resistant variety with the GA insensitive semi-dwarf rht-D1b gene.
the Czech varieties with the highest resistance to FHB were the varieties Bakfis and Federer, and that the presence of the r ht-D1a allele is not a limiting factor for resistance to FHB.

the resistance of the examined varieties to FHB was highly influenced by environmental conditions and that the presence of rht alleles in the examined genotypes had an effect on the expression of resistance, but this effect was not significant.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Czech wheat breeders should pay attention to the effect of rht alleles on FHB resistance in their breeding programs, and that the breeding for FHB resistance should be based on the combination of resistance to FHB and resistance to lodging.
the resistance of wheat to FHB is a complex phenomenon and that it cannot be evaluated on the basis of only one trait.
the presence of r ht-D2b and/or r ht-D3b is associated with a higher resistance to FHB, and that these alleles should be used in the development of new wheat varieties with a higher resistance.
